adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a new webhook endpoint at apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts that uses findFirst to check if a credential exists (lines 57-65), then either updates or creates based on the result (lines 67-85). This is a classic read-then-write race condition - two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same userId/appId could both see no existing credential and both attempt to create, leading to duplicate credentials or database errors. The code has no transaction wrapper, unique constraint enforcement, or upsert pattern to prevent this. While the rebuttal mentions webhook serialization, the code itself has no such protection and webhooks can indeed be delivered concurrently from retries or multiple senders.
